0.long_answer: Dercum's disease, also known as adiposis dolorosa, is a rare condition first described by Dr. Dercum, who notably served as President Woodrow Wilson's personal physician. It primarily affects women beginning in their third decade of life. The disease is characterized by the development of multiple painful fatty tumors (lipomas) which can appear throughout the subcutaneous fat. Additionally, individuals with Dercum's disease often experience obesity and fatigue. Although the exact cause remains unclear, this complex disorder is managed through a variety of approaches focused on alleviating pain and other associated symptoms.
